transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having a hard time with wasps. It’s gotten to where I plan most of my summer around avoiding them. I stopped helping with the garden work at church, and if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I make my husband unload things instead.
Do you ever have panic or a panic attack when you see a wasp or think you might see one?
Yes… I guess it feels like that. If I hear that sharp buzzing on the porch, or see one around the flowers, my heart kind of jumps and my hands shake. I just feel like I need to get inside right away.
Are you afraid of anything else besides wasps?
Not really… I mean, nothing that feels like this. It’s mostly the wasps.
Is it the wasp itself that scares you, or the possibility of being stung?

I think it’s more… being stung, or what might happen if it comes near me. I know it’s just a little insect, and other people don’t make such a fuss, but to me it feels like something awful is about to happen.
Have you avoided any other activities or places because of your fear of wasps?

Yes… I have. I don’t like admitting it, but I’ve started planning most of my summer around staying away from them. I stopped helping with the garden work at church, and if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I’ll make my husband unload things instead of going out there myself.
Have you ever avoided going outside at all during the summer because of your fear of wasps?

Yes… sometimes I just don’t go out if I think they’ll be around. In the summer I end up planning a lot around avoiding them, like skipping the garden work at church or asking my husband to deal with things by the back porch if I hear buzzing.
Is your fear more about the pain of being stung or the possibility of having a severe allergic reaction?

I don’t know if it’s exactly the pain or an allergy… it’s more that if one gets near me, I just feel like something terrible is going to happen. I know it’s only a wasp, but I can’t seem to feel that way in the moment.
Have you ever avoided social gatherings or events because of your fear of wasps?

Yes… I have skipped things, especially in the summer. If it’s outdoors or near where I think wasps might be, I’ll usually find a reason not to go. I’ve even stopped doing the garden jobs at church because of it.
Have you ever felt like your fear of wasps is interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Yes… I think it has. I’ve pulled back from the church gardening group, and I don’t host garden days anymore like I used to. My husband handles the porch and garden things now, mostly. It’s… embarrassing, really.
Have you considered seeking help for your fear of wasps before now?
Not really… I mean, I’ve thought maybe I should, but I never actually did anything about it until now.
Have you ever avoided going on vacation or traveling during the summer because of your fear of wasps?

Yes… I’ve planned a lot of my summer around avoiding them. I wouldn’t say it’s always a full vacation, but if there’s travel or staying somewhere outdoorsy, I get really reluctant. I’ve given up things like the garden work at church, and even at home I’ll have my husband unload things by the back porch if I hear buzzing.
Do you feel anxious or fearful around others when you're in a situation where wasps might be present?
Yes… I do. I know it’s just a little insect, and other people don’t make a fuss, but if I think there might be one nearby, I get scared like something awful is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps specifically about the possibility of being stung by a wasp that you know is present, or is it more about the general possibility of encountering a wasp somewhere?
It’s more the thought of one being around at all, I think. If I know one is near me… I just feel like something terrible could happen, even though I know most people would just swat it away.
Are you afraid of other insects, like bees or hornets, as well, or is it just wasps that scare you?

Mostly wasps. I mean… bees and hornets would make me uneasy too, I guess, but with wasps it’s different. If one gets near me, it feels like something terrible is about to happen, even though I know it’s just a little insect.
Do you feel the same level of fear when you see a bee or a hornet as you do when you see a wasp?
No… not the same. Bees or hornets would bother me, sure, but with a wasp it’s stronger. I know it’s just a little insect, but if one gets near me, it feels like something terrible is going to happen.
Do you think your fear would be just as bad if you saw a hornet instead of a wasp?

Probably not quite as bad. A hornet would scare me, but with a wasp… I know it’s small and most people would just deal with it, but if it gets near me I feel like something terrible is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps more about the act of being stung or about the wasp itself being present?
It’s… more the wasp being there, I think. I know it’s just a little insect and most people would swat it away, but if one gets near me, it feels like something terrible is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps worse when you're in a specific place, like your backyard, or is it the same no matter where you are?
It’s not really just one place. If a wasp gets close to me anywhere, I… I know it’s small and other people would just swat it away, but I feel like something awful is about to happen.
Is your fear of wasps always the same, or does it get worse when you're doing something specific, like gardening?

It’s worse when I’m doing things where I might run into them, yeah. I’ve kind of started planning my summer around avoiding them. I stopped helping with the garden work at church, and if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I’ll ask my husband to unload things instead.
